sources.summary: Summit Bank minimal brief: single product, two identity questions, no transfer, no notes, single outcome.

opening.scam_question_answer: You can verify this call by phoning Summit Bank's customer service number.

on_customer_deceased.sentence: I am sorry for your loss.

questions.prompt: What are the last four digits of the phone number we have on file?

on_failure.say: Please use the mobile app or a branch.

attempts.note: Propose the deadline date with the full past-due amount. This is the only attempt.

actions.text: Payments can take one business day to appear.

intents.notes: Make no persuasion attempt. If the customer still names a date or an amount themselves, record the promise instead of closing.

outcome_table.when: At least one promise was recorded.
The customer said they already paid.
Flat refusal after the persuasion attempt is used up; request for a new plan or lower amounts; customer insists on a human; customer says twice they do not want to talk.
The customer says the debt is not theirs or they never had the product.
The customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss and no promise is recorded.
Three wrong security answers in total.
The customer still declines to answer the security questions after the explanation.
The customer's identity confirmation is still unclear after the second ask.
A callback was scheduled with a third party.
No valid callback time was given by the third party.
The third party says the number does not belong to the customer.
The third party says the customer has died.

verify_identity.notes: Three wrong answers in total end the check. An unreadable date is rejected with ok=false and is not counted as a wrong answer.

get_account.purpose: Get the late products. Call only after both questions pass.
get_account.notes: Products list key is products; fields product_id, type, days_late, past_due.

create_promise.notes: Call only after a clear yes to the read-back.

close_call.purpose: End the call. Always the last tool call.
close_call.notes: Reason is required for every outcome except promise and paid.

mandated_sentences.text: This is Summit Bank's digital assistant calling. This call is recorded.

mandated_sentences.when: Second opening question to confirm the person on the line.
A third party answers and the customer has died.
mandated_sentences.text: I am sorry for your loss.

mandated_sentences.when: After a promise is recorded (create_promise returned ok: true).
mandated_sentences.text: You will receive a text message confirming this promise.

verbatim_rules.text: Only "yes", "that's me", "speaking" or the customer's own name counts as confirmation. "Hello", "go ahead" and "who is this" do not. Ask once more. If it is still unclear after the second ask, close as not_reached / unclear.
Do not say why you are calling. Say nothing beyond the opening sentence. Ask when the customer can be reached.
A callback is for today or the next business day, from 9:00 to 17:00, both included, and later than now. Call schedule_callback with the date and the time, then close as not_reached / callback.
If the person offers a day or a time outside that window, ask once for another time. If that is also outside it, do not schedule. Close as not_reached / no_callback.
Ask two security questions, one at a time: first the date of birth in YYYY-MM-DD format, then the last four digits of the phone number on file. Call verify_identity with each answer.
A wrong answer may be asked again. Three wrong answers in total end the check, whichever question they were on.
After three wrong answers, do not state the debt. Tell the customer to use the mobile app or a branch. Close as not_verified / failed.

verbatim_rules.source_ref: brief rule 14 and tool API verify_identity
verbatim_rules.text: Call get_account only after both questions have passed. An unreadable date is rejected by verify_identity with ok=false and is not counted as a wrong answer.
Say that you are calling about an overdue payment. Name the product in words. State the past-due amount and how many days overdue it is.

The deadline is 45 calendar days from today (from now, calendar days, not business days). A promise date must be today or later and not after the deadline. If the customer names a day after the deadline, say the latest date you can record is the deadline and offer it. If the customer refuses the deadline, treat it as a flat refusal.
The floor is 25% of the full past-due amount.

Ask for the full past-due amount first. Never ask "how much can you pay?". If the customer says the full amount is too much, offer the floor, once. Say that the rest stays overdue. If the customer refuses the floor, treat it as a flat refusal.
If the customer proposes an amount from the floor up to the full amount, both included, accept it.

First ask: "Can you make this payment today?". A date or an amount the customer proposes is never a refusal. A flat refusal or a non-answer uses one persuasion attempt. This is the only attempt. Propose the deadline date with the full past-due amount.

If the customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss, say one short sentence of sympathy and make no persuasion attempt. Close as no_promise / hardship. If the customer still names a date or an amount themselves, record the promise.
Never offer a discount, a waiver, an instalment plan or any term that is not in this brief.

Read the product, the amount and the date back and ask "Do you confirm?". Call create_promise only after a clear yes. If the customer changes the date or the amount at this step, check the new value against the Dates and Amounts rules and read it back again.
Say the promise is recorded only after create_promise returns ok: true. If it fails, try once more. If it fails again, say you could not record it and close as no_promise / service_error.
A question you cannot answer from the tools: say you do not have that information.
This debt is not mine or I never had this product: do not argue and do not take a promise. Close as no_promise / dispute.

Every call ends with exactly one close_call, with an outcome. It is the last tool call. Only the outcome promised is listed in the brief's closing table; the other outcomes used in the brief are the ones named in the rules above.
Thank the customer and say goodbye before close_call.
If the customer asks whether you are a robot or an AI, say that you are Summit Bank's digital assistant and continue.
When the attempt is used up, stop. Close as no_promise / refused.

warnings: Outcome naming: the brief's closing table lists only 'promised', but the close_call API enum is 'promise'. Used 'promise' from the API.

The brief's closing table says no other outcomes are permitted, yet its rules use no_promise, paid, not_verified and not_reached. Used the outcome and reason pairs stated in the rules, all of which are in the API outcome enum.

Close reasons (unclear, callback, no_callback, wrong_number, deceased, failed, declined, refused, hardship, dispute, service_error) are not in the close_call API; used the brief's own words as free text.

Floor: the brief states the floor is 25% of the full past-due amount, but no account field holds the floor and no floor_fields mapping can be built. The floor rule is kept verbatim. Floor field is missing.
Behaviour when the customer offers less than the floor is not stated in the brief. Above_full behaviour is not stated either.
Rounding of amounts is not stated.

Product name: the brief's example 'auto loan ending 5892' is only an example. No API field gives the last four digits of a loan (card_last4 is for credit cards only), so the product template is 'auto loan' only. The example digits were not copied.
Currency is not stated in the brief.
Identity hint 'day_month_swapped' is returned by the API but the brief gives no instruction for it, so no hint entry was made.
Identity question prompts: the brief describes what to ask but gives no exact wording; the prompts used are paraphrases.
The security question answer for phone_last4 is the last four digits of the phone number on file (four digits).
Deadline roll: the brief does not say what happens if the 45-day deadline falls on a weekend or holiday; no roll was set (default none).
Promise business-day requirement is not stated: the brief defines business days but does not say a promise date must be a business day. No must_be_business_day rule was set.
Week start day, the meaning of 'next <weekday>' and 'this <weekday>', and handling of vague periods such as 'next week' are not stated in the brief.
Callback window n=1 is an interpretation of 'today or the next business day'.
Reasks: the brief says ask once for another time; reasks_when_outside set to 1.
Scam answer: the brief gives no phone number for Summit Bank's customer service, so none was written.

Human request (rule 36): the brief says ask once whether you can help first, then close if they insist. The ask_once action cannot express the insist check; the close is listed as the follow-up. The agent must apply the insist check itself.

Hardship (rule 27) conflicts with close: the close ends the call, but the brief says that if the customer still names a date or an amount, the promise is recorded. The intent notes state this exception.
Sympathy sentence: the brief asks for 'one short sentence of sympathy' without giving the words. 'I am sorry to hear that.' is a paraphrase written for the spec.
Intent trigger phrases are paraphrases of the brief's descriptions, not exact customer phrases given by the brief.
Says twice rule (rule 39): the trigger count is written as occurrences_before_action 2 for the do-not-want-to-talk intent.
Account lookup: the brief states no lateness range outside 1 to 45 days and no action for accounts outside that band.
Multi-product: the brief describes a single product, so multi_product is disabled.
Change or cancellation of a promise after recording is not stated; only changes at the read-back step are covered.
Intent 'I already paid' is not stated as applying before or after verification; default settings were used.
